note: Adapted from Bacchus's (1997) original description (in English); only the soldier and the major worker are described; the original gives the alate as IMAGO. Unknown. The author distinguishes the soldier by its longer mandibles (0.55—0.58 mm, against 0.48—0.53 mm in similar species) and the worker as closest to mulii but with a shorter hind tibia (0.48—0.50 mm, against 0.50—0.55 mm in mulii).

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head capsule and labrum yellow to pale orange; mandibles brown to red-brown with a yellow base; antennae, body and legs pale yellow, the sides of the antennae brownish; postmentum yellow, slightly darker than the cheeks. Head capsule almost rectangular; sides parallel or slightly converging behind the antennal fossae; posterior margin evenly and slightly arcuately rounded. Sides with several long hairs and very short hairs; the pair of hairs on the frons very close together. Labrum narrowly tongue-shaped, with 3 pairs of hairs in the anterior third, the distal pair the longest, each more posterior pair about half as long as the long hairs. Tip of the mandibles moderately incurved, the degree of curvature 0.04—0.06 mm. Antennae 13-segmented, segment 3 the shortest, segment 4 slightly larger, segments 1 and 2 about equal. Postmentum short and wide. Pronotum saddle-shaped with several long hairs, the anterior margin with a small V-shaped notch, the posterior margin slightly concave and the angles rounded. Fore tibia slightly swollen; spurs 3, the dorsal spur as long as the outer ventral spur; a large hair on the front of the fore coxa almost spine-like.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Major worker: head capsule yellow to orange; mandibles brown with a yellow base; body, legs and antennae pale yellow; postclypeal pad red-brown. Head capsule almost rectangular, the sides nearly parallel, the posterior margin broad and evenly rounded. Head hairs moderately numerous and arranged symmetrically; postclypeus large and inflated, almost semicircular; anteclypeus flat, projecting forwards in the middle; the fork of the cranial suture only partly visible. Antennae 13-segmented, segments 3 and 4 about the same size, segments 1 and 2 about equal; labrum with a transverse sclerotized band, the tip broadly rounded; postmentum with several long hairs. Pronotum saddle-shaped, the middle of the anterior margin very slightly incurved, the posterior margin straight. Fore tibia not swollen; spurs 3, the dorsal spur almost as long as the outer ventral spur; a long hair on the front of the fore coxa not spine-like.

sections.label: Other
sections.text: Soldier measurements (12 specimens, 12 colonies, mm): head including the mandibles 1.38—1.55, head length to the base of the mandibles 0.88—1.00, head width behind the antennal fossae 0.68—0.75, greatest head width 0.69—0.80, labrum length 0.28—0.33 and width 0.19—0.21, left mandible transverse length 0.55—0.58, width 0.05, curvature 0.04—0.06, fore tibia length 0.45—0.53 and width 0.10—0.13, hind tibia length 0.55—0.60 and width 0.08—0.10, greatest pronotum width 0.48—0.53, postmentum length 0.48—0.50, greatest width 0.33—0.35. Major worker measurements (9 specimens, 9 colonies): head length to the anterior margin of the postclypeus 0.88—1.00, greatest head width 0.75—0.80, postclypeal pad length 0.25—0.26 and width 0.38—0.41, greatest pronotum width 0.38—0.45, fore tibia length 0.38—0.45 and width 0.08—0.09, hind tibia length 0.48—0.50 and width 0.06—0.08. Soldier holotype from Maktau, western Tsavo Park, Kenya, 1 November (month 11) 1988 (Bacchus, Bagine, NMK). Colonies were taken from the trunk of a rotting baobab, from old sisal stumps and from maize stubble in cultivated land.
